newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Consortium signs $50-mln deal with US,Russia firms.
newsitem.headline: Consortium signs $50-mln deal with US,Russia firms.

text.p: The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) signed a $50 million deal with a consortium of Fluor Daniel of the United States and Russia's Girpovostokneft Institute to work on the CPC's oil export pipeline system, the CPC said on Thursday.
Giprovostokneft is a leading designer of oil and gas field and pipeline systems in Russia and Kazakhstan, and Fluor Daniel is an upstream oil and gas service firm.
Fluor Daniel is the principal subsidiary of Fluor Corp, a global engineering and contruction company, the CPC said in a statement.

CPC plans to build a $2-billion, 1,500-kilometre (935-mile) pipeline system from Kazakhstan's Tengiz oil field to Russia's Black Sea export outlet of Novorossiisk, with eventual capacity aimed at 1.5 million barrels per day, it said.

When the group restructuring is complete, Russia will own 24 percent of CPC, Kazakhstan 19 percent, Oman seven percent, Chevron Corp of the United States 15 percent, LUKoil of Russia 12.5 percent, Mobil of the United States 7.5 percent, Rosneft of Russia 7.5 percent, Italy's Agip and British Gas two percent each, and Oryx Energy Company and Kazakhstan's Munaigaz 1.75 percent each.
